overview: Three internal sub-sectors: (a) Water Sourcing/Supply & Groundwater Management, (b) Municipal Wastewater Management, (c) Urban Drainage and Urban Flooding.
current_situation: Primary water source Pawana Dam (550 MLD) + Andra Dam (80 MLD) + MIDC (20 MLD). Water demand projected to rise from 666 MLD (2025) to 1,709 MLD by 2041. Non-Revenue Water > 40%. Sewage generation projected to reach 1,272.39 MLD by 2040 (projected population 9,617,435). Drainage: ~228 km nalla network (153 km major, 93 km minor); ~61 open nallas into Indrayani river (8 polluted), ~38 into Pawana river; 88 piped + 60+ natural outfalls into Mula/Mutha rivers.
challenges: Non-Revenue Water > 40%; 24x7 water-supply pilot initiated but not implemented
No city-level aquifer maps or groundwater extraction data available yet
Groundwater over-exploitation, especially in areas like Pimple Saudagar
Poorly planned sewer network lacking design norms/hydraulic calculations
6 piped outfalls discharge untreated sewage directly into the Indrayani river
Land constraints for new STPs; old STPs cannot meet NGT/MPCB/CPCB standards
Encroachment on nallas causing monsoon spillover; haphazard riverside development
existing_initiatives: 24x7 water supply pilot project initiated (not yet implemented citywide)
PCMC map of groundwater recharge areas

strategies.name: Develop a city-wide climate-resilient water-supply master plan.
Conduct participatory aquifer mapping and develop an Aquifer Management Plan.
Implement demand management, NRW reduction, and water conservation measures.
Expand sewerage coverage and upgrade sewerage network infrastructure.
Expand sewage treatment capacity and enhance treatment quality.
Implement wastewater recycling/reuse (WWRR) plan - target >=100 MLD reuse by 2035.
Integrate renewable energy at plant premises; resource recovery.
Deploy real-time monitoring, PLC & SCADA across all STPs.
Map, restore and retain natural nalla systems integrated with rivers/lakes.
Identify and map river outfalls; pollution abatement measures.
Map, plan and integrate Blue-Green Infrastructure (BGI) / sponge-city concept.
Identify flood hotspots, map, validate, implement mitigation measures.
Raise awareness and behavioural change to reduce pollution of water bodies.
